title: kv-cache: adaptive-eviction-and-spillover-paging-v2
author: Aisha Raman
description:
Motivation: OOMs and fragmentation remain a recurring pain for large batched workloads—especially long-context chat sessions that trigger heavy KV cache growth and irregular eviction patterns. This PR implements an adaptive eviction pipeline that combines fragmentation-aware free-list compaction, a lightweight paging/spillover mechanism, and scheduling hints to reduce eviction chatter and tail latency.

Summary of changes: consolidated the kv cache memory manager into a single adaptive controller; added fragmentation scoring per slab and per-model; background compaction path that coalesces small free fragments into larger pages; spillover paging that increments an age-based weight to cold entries and moves them to a reclaimed spill file when memory pressure is high; scheduling integration that delays non-critical batch prefetches when compaction is running.

Design notes: the controller tracks per-slab fragmentation ratio and eviction churn. When fragmentation > 0.35 and churn > threshold, the controller ramps compaction for that slab and marks entries eligible for paging. Paging is implemented as an append-only spill file per GPU instance with a compact index kept in RAM. Evicted keys get a lightweight descriptor in the index; on hot access the descriptor triggers an async page-in. The design favors low-latency fast-path reads (no page checks unless miss counts exceed a small threshold). We tuned the spill file sync frequency to amortize write latency across multiple evictions.

Compatibility: backwards-compatible with existing kv cache format (index version bump + migration path). Config flags added: kv.adaptive_eviction.enabled, kv.spillover.enabled, kv.compaction.batch_ms. Defaults keep previous behavior off for Dedicated customers; rollout via feature flag.

Testing & results: microbenchmarks with multi-session long-context chat (avg seq_len 8192 across 96 concurrent sessions) show:  - 30% reduction in OOMs during synthetic stress tests  - 12% increase in sustained throughput under mixed-length traffic  - 18% reduction in P90 tail latency for token generation when compaction is active  - Spill file write amplification measured at ~1.08x under normal load, tuned via sync window.

Rollout plan: feature-flag gated. Start with a 5% traffic canary for hosted API + Dedicated staging pools, monitor kv.free_frag_ratio, eviction_churn, page_fault_rate, and P95 latency. If regression detected, auto-fallback to legacy eviction.

Notes: This change touched runtime kernel alignment in a few places (aligned free-list objects to 64 bytes) — see small kernel tweaks in runtime/memory_kernels.cu. Benchmarks added under perf-canary and new unit/integration tests under eval-harness.

Related: ENG-2345 (kv cache reliability epic), SUP-9812 (customer-reported OOMs).

review_comments: Connor Lee: Nice overall. Two concerns: (1) spill file durability semantics under preemption, (2) async page-in backpressure. Please add a short note and a test for OOM during page-in.
Aisha Raman: Addressed both — spill file now uses instance-local WAL+rename on rotate; added backpressure window and test that simulates preemption. See commit c3d4e5 and e5f6a7.
Marta Iglesias: Can we make compaction scheduler more conservative under latency-sensitive routes? Suggest adding scheduling hints from router.
Aisha Raman: Added scheduling hint integration (router route metadata -> kv.compaction.priority). Default is unchanged; documented in redwood-docs.
Devon Park: Approve after CI passes and perf numbers verified in perf-canary.
CI Bot: All checks passed (build + unit + integration + perf-canary).
ci_checks: perf-canary: pass (12% throughput up, 18% P90 down)
changelog: kv-cache: add adaptive eviction controller, fragmentation-aware compaction, and spillover paging; config flags and rollout notes included
release_notes: Improves KV cache resilience under long-context, high-concurrency workloads. Reduces OOMs and tail latency by using adaptive compaction and optional spillover paging. Feature gated; enable via kv.adaptive_eviction.enabled.
notes_for_ops: Watch metrics: kv.free_frag_ratio, kv.eviction_churn, kv.page_fault_rate, kv.spill_write_latency. Rollback via kv.adaptive_eviction.enabled=false or disable spillover.
regression_risks: Kernel alignment changes can affect memory layout; test coverage added. Spill file IO could increase disk usage under extreme churn—monitor spill_file_size and io_wait.
testing_summary: Unit tests for compaction and index, integration test for async page-in, perf-canary runs with synthetic long-context traffic. Backpressure and preemption scenarios covered in tests.
how_reviewed: Code review by runtime team (Connor, Marta), perf verification by perf-canary, security sign-off not required for this change (no new network surfaces).
author_response_to_review: Addressed comments: added WAL+rotate for spill files, added backpressure window, integrated scheduling hints, and added docs + helm values for toggling.
auditing: Added audit log events for spill file rotations and page-in events (runtime/kv/audit.cpp).
notes: Follow-up work: auto-tiering of spill files to slower storage, index compaction to avoid memory growth over long uptimes.
